fields.meta_description: A salon landing page sells one visit. See four salon examples and build one that saves every booking request to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Salon Landing Page That Fills the Chair
fields.hero_description: Build a salon landing page with your service prices, a short request form, and every booking saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Salon Page Needs Before Booking
fields.features_subheading: A salon landing page sells one visit and turns a visitor into a booking request. Six parts do that work, and each changes by prompt.
fields.feature_1:
A service menu with a price on each line

List each service with its time and price, such as a gloss for $65 in 45 minutes. Emergent builds the menu from your prompt, and a new price is one more message to the page.
fields.feature_2:
A request form that asks for a time window

Ask for a name, a phone number, the service, and whether a weekend or weekday suits the visitor. The front desk then calls each visitor back to confirm the exact time and stylist.
fields.feature_3:
Booking rules written in plain words

Describe a rule the way you would tell a new hire: a lash fill past 4 weeks books as a full set. Emergent writes the rule into the page, and you change it later by prompting again.
fields.feature_4:
Every request saved as a row you own

Each request lands as a row in a database you own, with the service, the window, and the stylist the visitor picked. Sort the rows by week or by stylist, and call back from the list.
fields.feature_5:
An alert the moment a request comes in

Send each new request to the front desk by email, in Slack, or as an in-app alert. Pick who gets which service, so a color request reaches the colorist and a barber gets the cuts.
fields.feature_6:
Your page on your domain, or as code

Host the page on Emergent under your own domain (custom domains use credits). Or export the page and its request table to your GitHub repository on paid plans and own the code.

fields.usecase_heading: Salon Landing Page Examples by Studio Type
fields.tab_content_1:
The $25 first-visit offer asks for a window, not a slot

Copperline Color Studio sells one visit on this page: $25 off a first color appointment. The request form ends on a single question, weekend or weekday. This month 52 requests came in. 33 picked a weekend and 19 picked a weekday, and each one is a row the front desk books from.
fields.tab_content_2:
Three seats held from one phone

Juniper Nail Studio takes groups in one request. Its page lets one person hold up to 4 seats at the same start time. Imogen Vale held 3 seats for Friday at 5:30 pm from her phone. Each seat landed as its own row under her contact, with a blank for the guest's name.
fields.tab_content_3:
The calendar decides fill or full set

Alder Lash Co. prices by the calendar. A fill requested more than 4 weeks after the last visit books as a $120 full set instead of a $45 fill. Mirela Sanz asked for a fill 5 weeks after her last visit. The page offered her the full set and saved her request with both dates.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every open chair goes to the next name

Fadewell Barbershop's page lets a visitor join the walk-in list from the sidewalk and shows the wait the front desk quotes, 40 minutes on this Saturday. When a barber marks a chair open, the next name on the list gets an email. Dario Vance was next at 2:15 pm.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Salon Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a salon landing page that sells one visit, prices it plainly, and routes every request to a named person.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the one visit the page sells
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Price the work where it is read
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask when the visitor is free
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Name the person behind the chair
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose a single visit, such as a first color appointment or a lash fill, and build the page around it. A visitor who tapped an ad for balayage should land on balayage, not on the full menu of every service the salon offers.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the price and the time next to each service, in the same line. A visitor choosing between a gloss and a full color should see both numbers before asking for a visit. Leave out "prices vary" unless the page says what they vary by.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Unless the page reads the salon's real calendar, ask for a weekend or a weekday, morning or evening, and let the front desk confirm the time. Keep the form to four fields so it fits on one phone screen.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Show each stylist's name, photo and specialty, and let the visitor pick one or choose the first available. Keep the pick in the request row: it tells the front desk whose book to fill first.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide what the page does with the edge cases before it goes live: a fill past 4 weeks, a group bigger than the seats you hold, a request for a service on a day it is not offered. Describe each rule in one sentence.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send each request to the right person
fields.howto_step_6_des: Route color requests to the colorist, lash requests to the lash artist, and walk-ins to the front desk. Send one test request for each service and check who got it, before any ad points traffic at the page.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Mark the page up as a local business
fields.howto_step_7_des: Add LocalBusiness structured data with the salon's name, address and phone number. Google's guidance says to use the most specific LocalBusiness sub-type possible, and schema.org lists HairSalon and NailSalon under HealthAndBeautyBusiness. Add the opening hours in the same markup.

faq_plan.q: What is a salon landing page?
faq_plan.a: A salon landing page is a single web page that sells one salon visit, such as a first cut or a lash fill, and asks the visitor for a booking request. It carries the service, its price, the stylists, and a short request form, and leaves the full menu to the main site.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a salon landing page?
faq_plan.a: Decide which visit the page sells, then describe it in a prompt: the service, the price, the stylists, and the questions on the request form. Emergent's AI landing page builder builds the page and a table for the requests, and you change any part by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: What should a salon landing page include?
faq_plan.a: Include one service with its price and duration, photos of real work, the stylists who do it, the address and opening hours, and a request form of four or five fields. Put the form and the phone number where a visitor sees them without scrolling on a phone.

faq_plan.q: Can a salon landing page take group bookings for weddings or company events?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for the date, the number of people and the service each person wants, then hold the seats as separate rows under one contact. For a company booking a team day, borrow three parts from a b2b landing page: who it is for, what is included, and one named contact.

faq_plan.q: Should a salon landing page show prices?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for the service the page sells. List what the visit costs and how long it takes, and say plainly when the price depends on hair length or the stylist's level. If the price varies, give a starting price and the reason it can change.

faq_plan.q: Do I need a salon landing page if I already use a booking app?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when you want to sell one offer to one audience. A landing page takes a visitor from an ad or a post straight to that offer, before a full calendar of every service. On Emergent, each request lands in a table you own, next to the offer that brought it in.

faq_plan.q: How do I get new clients from a salon landing page?
faq_plan.a: Give first-time visitors a reason to ask, such as $25 off a first color visit, and keep the form to contact details and a preferred day. A lead generation landing page makes the same trade: an offer for contact details.

faq_plan.q: Do I need a template to build a salon landing page?
faq_plan.a: No. Emergent builds the page from a prompt, so you can start from a description of the salon instead of a layout: the services, the stylists, and what the request form asks. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: How should a hair salon landing page show the stylists' work?
faq_plan.a: Show before and after photos of real clients who agreed to it. Label each photo with the service and the stylist who did it. Put three to six photos near the price, and swap them as the season's work changes.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a separate salon landing page for each location?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each location its own page with its own address, phone number, hours, and stylists. Each request then reaches the right shop. A real estate landing page follows the same rule with one page per listing. Paid plans export each page's code to your GitHub repository.

plan.angle: The top 10 for salon landing page is design galleries and template lists (Figma, Behance, Dribbble, Embeddable, Nicepage) plus two booking-strategy guides: they show what a salon page looks like, never what happens after the request button. This page shows four salon types (a hair color studio, a nail studio, a brow and lash studio, a barbershop), each page built around one booking moment with the request form, the rule or alert behind it, and the database row it lands in. The spa landing page is a sibling and stays out of the headings; the booking form itself belongs to the Form hub and is never a heading here.
